steps.title: Aragón
steps.body: In Aragón, Garnacha's likely birthplace, Campo de Borja, Calatayud and Cariñena have many old bush vines on poor, stony soils. Campo de Borja calls itself the empire of Garnacha. These areas once made bulk wine but now offer concentrated, good-value Garnacha.

steps.title: Priorat and Gredos
steps.body: In Priorat, old Garnacha and Cariñena on llicorella slate make powerful, mineral wines. In the Sierra de Gredos, west of Madrid, old Garnacha vines on granite at 600 to 1,200 m were rediscovered in the 2000s. Gredos Garnacha is pale, fragrant and fresh, often compared with Burgundy.

steps.prompt: Match each Spanish area to its Garnacha.
steps.explanation: Spain shows every side of Garnacha.

steps.body: Gredos Garnacha shows a lighter, more elegant face of the grape. Try one next to a Châteauneuf to see how much altitude and granite change it.

steps.prompt: Why is Gredos Garnacha often fresher than other Garnachas?
steps.explanation: Altitude up to 1,200 m and granite give freshness and perfume.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Aragón is Garnacha's homeland, with old bush vines
Priorat makes powerful Garnacha on slate
Gredos makes fragrant, fresh Garnacha at altitude
